findings.problem: The Hindi wording for open biodiversity access omitted the biodiversity qualifier and could be read as generic open access.
findings.resolution_required: Restore explicit biodiversity-data scope while preserving the federated and formal-governance meaning.

findings.problem: Global federation and discover/search wording could be made more explicit and less redundant.
Commons and self-governance terminology could be made more natural and agentive in Hindi.
Neighbourhood collective agency and the internal-sewer versus public trunk-infrastructure contrast could be expressed more directly.

limitations: Model-assisted independent review only; no native-speaker or human Hindi approval is claimed.
Scope was limited to the three newly added Hindi project overlays and their canonical English/German meanings.
